nodes.norm_label: opencode v2 plugin contract breaks v1-era plugins
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-ai-skills/2026-10-01 - graphify-js-plugin-export-fix [ses_f07e83b71ffeqlRc6yhQ313p17].md:L07584] Rewrote it to `export default { id: "graphify", async setup(ctx) {...} }` with the hook registered via `ctx.tool.hook("execute.before", ...)` and `event.input.command` mutation (confirmed against the V2 plugin docs and migration guide).
nodes.summary: Reused id, third owner (chunk-rem-024 found the V1 form still shipping and routed around it via MCP; chunk-rem-089 migrated rtk.ts off it). Here the failing plugin is ~/ai-skills/.opencode/plugins/graphify.js and the same V1 shape is migrated rather than routed around.

nodes.label: A bare plugin file has no node_modules, so a runtime import from @opencode/plugin cannot resolve
nodes.norm_label: a bare plugin file has no node_modules for a runtime import
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-ai-skills/2026-10-01 - graphify-js-plugin-export-fix [ses_f07e83b71ffeqlRc6yhQ313p17].md:L7585] my first version imported `Plugin` from `@opencode/plugin`, which can't resolve from a bare `.js` file (`Cannot find package` in the log). Dropped it; a plain object is all V2 requires. The server log at L5739/L5742 shows the same failure twice as `failed to load plugin ... ref=err_79cd1c44` and `err_ea067325`, both `Die(ResolveMessage: Cannot find package '@opencode/plugin' ...)`, which is how the plugin was diagnosed as broken rather than as absent.
nodes.summary: Reused id, second owner. The failing file here is a .js plugin under a project .opencode/plugins/ rather than a .ts under ~/.config/opencode/plugins/, and the note states the same rule as a comment written into the file itself at L5965: a bare file has no node_modules above it to resolve from, so the default export is a plain object with id + setup.

nodes.label: A plugin entry in opencode.json is unnecessary, and a relative path in it is read as an npm package spec
nodes.norm_label: a plugin entry in opencode.json is unnecessary because plugins are auto-discovered
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-ai-skills/2026-10-01 - graphify-js-plugin-export-fix [ses_f07e83b71ffeqlRc6yhQ313p17].md:L7586] `.opencode/opencode.json` used the V1 `"plugin"` key (later `"plugins"` with a relative path, which the server also misread as an npm spec). Deleted the file; local plugins under `.opencode/plugins/` auto-load. The reason the relative path is worse than nothing is written into the deleted file at L6027: a relative path entry makes the server also try it as an npm package spec, which only adds NpmInstallFailedError warnings.
nodes.summary: The third and last of the three defects in the same file, and the only one where the fix was deletion rather than rewriting. Distinct from the export-shape and module-resolution bugs: nothing about the plugin source was wrong here, only the registry entry naming it.

nodes.label: A file the agent only ever read was rewritten on disk mid-session by an unattributed writer
nodes.norm_label: a file the agent only read was rewritten mid-session by an unattributed writer
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-ai-skills/2026-10-01 - graphify-js-plugin-export-fix [ses_f07e83b71ffeqlRc6yhQ313p17].md:L7590] `~/.config/opencode/plugins/rtk.ts` changed on disk mid-session (was 3.4K with a V2 `export default`, now 1339 bytes of old V1-style code importing `@opencode-ai/plugin`). I only ever read that file — something else rewrote it, and it now fails with the same LoadError class (`err_7e3d8681`, `err_07b773b8`). Reported, not fixed: it was outside this session's scope.
nodes.summary: Found by size and md5 disagreement rather than by any tool reporting a conflict — the session's own edits to graphify.js were tracked, and rtk.ts was only ever read, so its shrinking from 3.4K to 1339 bytes is attributable to nothing in the session. Same failure class as the bug it was fixing, which is what made it worth flagging rather than dismissing as unrelated.

nodes.label: A zombie chunk that stayed silent and then overwrote a re-chunked task's files
nodes.norm_label: a zombie chunk that stayed silent and then overwrote a re-chunked task files
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-26 - t4-id-page [ses_f2129c1dfffeeeXkUd0qIbZFuQ].md:L05941] While I was still editing it, **a concurrent agent replaced the file at 00:59:17** with a data-driven version that imports `@/data/solutions/social-media.id.ts` and creates the 8-icon `ICONS` map. My copy is gone from disk.
nodes.summary: Reused id, and this is the primary witness rather than the retrospective: chunk-rem-020 recorded the same event from the parent session's side as 'T4 lama tidak mati, hanya diam, lalu menimpa file yang sama dengan T4 re-chunk'. The overwrite was caught here by the file's own mtime (00:59:17.968959419) differing from the agent's last write, and by content the agent never wrote appearing in a file it still held write scope over.

nodes.label: When a concurrent agent replaces your file, verify their version against the contract instead of restoring yours
nodes.norm_label: when a concurrent agent replaces your file, verify their version against the contract instead of restoring your own
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-26 - t4-id-page [ses_f2129c1dfffeeeXkUd0qIbZFuQ].md:L05944] `docs/code-plan/plans/2026-09-27-solutions-social-media-landing.md:303-318` defines T4 as **"Halaman ID plus modul data (RE-CHUNKED setelah stall)"**, producing *both* `src/data/solutions/social-media.id.ts` (fixture) and the page as a "renderer tipis, target di bawah 300 baris", with FAQ/JSON-LD/table/workflows moved into the module.
nodes.summary: The agent held strict write scope for exactly one file, could rewrite it in seconds, and chose not to. The decision rule is separable from the overwrite itself: audit the peer's version against every hard contract string first, and let the authoritative plan decide whose architecture is correct rather than the brief that is now stale.

nodes.label: prettier cannot parse .astro at all because prettier-plugin-astro is absent
nodes.norm_label: prettier cannot parse astro at all because prettier plugin astro is absent
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-26 - t4-id-page [ses_f2129c1dfffeeeXkUd0qIbZFuQ].md:L05969] **Check 5 is not runnable in this workspace, not a formatting failure.** `prettier-plugin-astro` is not installed anywhere (`ls -d node_modules/prettier-plugin-astro` finds nothing; `apps/website/package.json` has no prettier script), and the pre-existing tracked baseline `src/pages/id/solutions/marketing.astro` fails with the identical error.
nodes.summary: Reused id, and this session's contribution is the baseline test rather than the diagnosis: the identical `No parser could be inferred` failure on an untouched tracked file is what separates 'the check cannot run' from 'this file is badly formatted', and it is why exit 2 was reported as not-runnable instead of as a formatting defect.

nodes.label: Copy-level requirements become unverifiable once the copy moves out of the page into a data module
nodes.norm_label: copy requirements become unverifiable once copy moves to a data module
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-26 - t4-id-page [ses_f2129c1dfffeeeXkUd0qIbZFuQ].md:L06007] The bend in the shipped file is architectural: the re-chunked T4 moved my brief's "local faqs array" and inline comparison table into `src/data/solutions/social-media.id.ts`, so all copy-level requirements (buzzer vocabulary, honesty block completeness, Indonesian proofreading) are now unverifiable and unfixable from the page file alone.
nodes.summary: The narrow claim under the thin-renderer architecture: splitting copy into a fixture satisfies the line-count and parity guards while making prose requirements uncheckable by the file they were written for. Concretely, the fixture's own header comment asserts the buzzer vocabulary is kept, and grep counts 1 occurrence in the fixture against 0 in user-facing copy.
